svg.title: Heterozygote advantage in sickle cell and malaria
svg.desc: Three boxes for the three genotypes where malaria is common. HbA HbA: normal hemoglobin and red blood cells, severe malaria more likely, fitness high but reduced by malaria. HbA HbS, the carrier: mostly normal hemoglobin, little or no sickling, strong protection against severe malaria, the highest fitness. HbS HbS: sickle hemoglobin only, cells sickle when oxygen is low, sickle cell disease, low fitness without medical care. Selection removes HbS through HbS HbS individuals and HbA through malaria deaths of HbA HbA individuals, so both alleles stay common: heterozygote advantage, a form of balancing selection.

g.text: Where malaria is common, carriers of one sickle-cell allele have the highest fitness
Cells sickle when O₂ is low
Selection removes HbS in HbS HbS individuals and HbA in malaria deaths of HbA HbA individuals,
so both alleles stay common: heterozygote advantage (balancing selection).
